reading.thesis: Heliod manufactures a resource nobody at the table prices -- cards in opponents' hands -- and six permanents read it (Consecrated Sphinx and Faerie Mastermind for cards, Gleaming Splendor and Smothering Tithe for Treasure, Scrawling Crawler for life loss, Heliod's back face as a cost discount); but the only win the deck is BUILT around is one seven-mana sorcery cast twice -- the output stage kills rarely -- and the goldfish that finds no kill by turn ten in 89.4% of games runs with five of those six readers DARK and the sixth given no cost channel.

open_questions.question: While Greater Auramancy is on the battlefield, Heliod has shroud from "other enchantments you control have shroud". Can Karametra's Blessing or Guardian of Faith's enters-trigger still be aimed at him, and if not, what is left to save him from Day of Judgment, Supreme Verdict or an opponent's wrath?
open_questions.why_it_matters: V12 swapped Lightning Greaves out for Greater Auramancy. Auramancy's own reminder text reads "(A permanent with shroud can't be the target of spells or abilities.)" with no opponent qualifier, and goldfish_targets' _v140_note already asserts the exclusion -- but no stack has cited it. If shroud blocks your own targeting, two of the four other members of the declared protection group cannot protect the commander while Auramancy is out, and the component reads a hand holding both as doubly covered when they partly exclude each other. Teferi's Protection does not target and is unaffected.

open_questions.question: Does Gleaming Splendor's trigger fire once per opponent per turn (three times a turn with three opponents), and if you activate its own "{2}{W}: Two target players each draw a card" targeting an opponent who has already drawn once this turn, does that card count as their second and trigger it?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The whole case for the swap is that the second-card trigger fires on three seats every turn the engine runs. The goldfish has already CHOSEN a reading -- goldfish_turn.py makes GOLDFISH_OPPONENTS Treasure per simulated turn when opponent_draws_this_turn >= 2 -- so a stack would check an implemented reading, not just a rules question. The self-feeding activation would make the card an ignition piece and a converter in one, or not, depending on ordering. Forge has cast the card in one run only (branch splendor-v1, 1b132fbb: 9 casts in 40 games, seat sha badd46c9, not this list), and engine_casts carries no trigger count.

open_questions.question: Does Heliod, the Warped Eclipse's cost reduction let you choose a larger X on Braingeyser, Stroke of Genius, Prosperity, Skyscribing, Mathemagics, Secure the Wastes, Walking Ballista or Hangarback Walker -- and is X chosen before or after the reduction applies?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The declared component 'An X-spell finisher drawn (the mana sink the discount pays for)' assembles 0.838 and its entire justification is this interaction. Nothing on disk tests it and the conversion->fuel line in this artifact rests on it.

open_questions.question: Can the second Approach of the Second Sun be cast at an opponent's end step under Heliod's back-face flash grant or Leyline of Anticipation, and is Fierce Guardianship's alternative cost live in that window when Heliod himself is the commander on the battlefield?
open_questions.why_it_matters: In Forge b0f44e4a (v1.2.1, seat 214af308), 12 of 120 games were won by Approach's effect; the run records no second-cast count at all, so the number of games that reached a second cast is twelve or more and is unmeasured. Anything that widens that window is the highest-leverage rules question this deck has. Stack 002 resolves only the sorcery-speed cast on your own turn.

open_questions.question: If model_treasures and model_discard are switched on for heliod, what do Gleaming Splendor, Smothering Tithe, Consecrated Sphinx, Faerie Mastermind, Rhystic Study and both Crawlers add to mana, draw and damage -- and how much of that rests on the authored TITHE_PAY_RATE (0.5) rather than on a measured rate?
open_questions.why_it_matters: WITHDRAWN: the previous question's premise, 'the goldfish has no opponents'. Since 2026-10-04 it seats GOLDFISH_OPPONENTS = 3 and reads opponent-draw Treasure and opponent-draw payoffs; model-coverage names seven DARK cards on exactly those two channels, five of them in the conversion stage. So every goldfish figure in this artifact is the deck measured with its engine switched off. Smothering Tithe's tax and Rhystic Study's are decided at TITHE_PAY_RATE, which config.py labels an authored assumption; OPPONENT_CASTS_PER_TURN (1.264) is measured. A figure resting on the first must say so.

open_questions.question: No declared target measures the deck's actual win: Approach of the Second Sun in hand AND seven mana available on two separate turns. Can the harness express a mana condition or a repeat cast, or must the gap be recorded?
open_questions.why_it_matters: 'Win condition access' assembles 0.560 by counting a hand that DREW Approach, Mystical Tutor or Long-Term Plans. Forge run b0f44e4a (v1.2.1, seat 214af308) records 39 casts across 120 games and 12 wins attributed to Approach's effect, with no second-cast counter anywhere in the record -- so the quantity this deck lives on is the one quantity no instrument on the bench reports. The component measures DRAWING one of three cards; nothing on the bench measures casting one card twice.

open_questions.question: Stack 002's scenario board lists Ancient Tomb, which is not in the current 99 (or in any list since v1.0.0). Does the resolution still hold on the V12 mana base, where {6}{W} has to come from 33 lands with no fast mana beyond Sol Ring?
open_questions.why_it_matters: 002 is the ONLY checker-passed stack on this deck, and all three of the verified pairings engine-facts lists come out of it. Its rules conclusion is about timing and does not depend on the board, but a reader who sees the board will read the mana as achievable when the deck's own goldfish says seven mana arrives between turn 7 and turn 8.

open_questions.question: In a four-player pod, how many tutor and protection slots is a single 'you win the game' card worth -- and given a 0-2 logged record and a goldfish that finds no kill by turn ten in 89.4% of games, should this deck hold a second, board-based route to a win at all?
open_questions.why_it_matters: strategic_frame.json already records that the corpus has NO section on alternate win conditions, and names strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window as the nearest -- written for board kills that leave a rebuilt position if they fail, which Approach cannot do. deck-audit's threat-density axis reads AT with three copies, so the disagreement is about the CLASS and not the count: two of the three it counts are drains, both DARK in the goldfish. The output stage produces value rather than a clock, and the 0.894 no-kill reading is combat-only.

findings.note: ROUND-4 OMISSION RESOLVED. Faerie Mastermind's activation is now listed. cards.json oracle reads '{3}{U}: Each player draws a card', with no timing restriction. I re-checked every listed card: The Second Doctor ('At the beginning of your end step, each player may draw a card'); Scrawling Crawler ('At the beginning of your upkeep, each player draws a card'); Prosperity ('Each player draws X cards', a sorcery); Skyscribing ('Each player draws X cards', with forecast 'Activate only during your upkeep'); Gleaming Splendor ('{2}{W}: Two target players each draw a card'). All are correct. I swept all 85 cards.json entries again with an oracle regex covering 'each player draws', 'may draw', 'its controller', 'target opponent each', 'target players each' and 'target player draws'. Nothing else hands an opponent a card. Path to Exile, Swords to Plowshares, Swan Song and An Offer You Can't Refuse give their controller a basic land, life, a Bird or Treasure, not cards. Archmage's Charm, Braingeyser, Stroke of Genius and Mathemagics ('Target player draws ...') stay out by the round-4 reasoning: aiming them at an opponent is not this deck's plan.

findings.claim: Arcane Denial if the next upkeep is yours
findings.note: The clause is correct as worded. cards.json oracle: 'Counter target spell. Its controller may draw up to two cards at the beginning of the next turn's upkeep.' The draw happens in the upkeep of the turn after Denial resolves, so it lands on your turn exactly when Denial resolves during the turn of the player seated before you. The spell countered can be any player's. That is what 'if the next upkeep is yours' says. Caution for the coordinator: the gloss 'if you counter the opponent seated before you' is looser than the model. What matters is WHOSE TURN Denial resolves on, not whose spell it counters. Countering that player's instant on another opponent's turn gives the draw to a different upkeep. The model's wording is the exact one; do not let a later revision swap in the gloss.

Measured: len() = 1798, inside the 1,800 cap with two characters to spare. The stage is not muddled; it reads in four labelled paragraphs. But it has no room left: the next revision of this stage must cut before it adds. A mechanical cap check already exists. This is a warning, not a finding against the model.

THE GOLDFISH AND THE BENCHMARK ARE ON THE CURRENT LIST (decklist f7e21dc6, model_version f5b4b19d2254) AND DO NOT READ THE SAME, because their harnesses differ: goldfish kill_by_turn_10 0.106, no kill by turn ten 0.894; benchmark kill_by_turn_10 0.112, never_kills_rate 0.888; both kill_by_turn_6 0.000, kill_by_turn_8 0.003, median kill turn 10. WITHDRAWN: 'so the gap is not a price on Treasure'. benchmark.json's harness is {model_treasures: true, model_combat: true}; goldfish_targets.json is {model_draw: true, model_combat: true}. They differ on two flags in opposite directions, so the 0.006 gap cannot be put down to either one, and it is unpaired. A goldfish has no blockers and nothing removes anything, so these are CEILINGS on combat -- and the drains are not in them at all. The captain's log is 0 wins and 2 losses, and log 001's cause -- 'I cast Swords to Plowshares, Alex redirected it onto Heliod. Engine offline from there' -- is precisely the failure Greater Auramancy answers.

WHAT THIS DECK HAS NO STAGE FOR. There is no `fodder` STAGE: no card in the 99 is played in order to be sacrificed, and nothing pays off when a permanent you own dies. The absolute sentence the previous model wrote -- 'nothing in the 99 sacrifices a resource it owns' -- is WITHDRAWN, because enumeration over cards.json oracle text falsifies it. Six entries carry the word 'sacrifice' at all: An Offer You Can't Refuse and Smothering Tithe only inside Treasure-token reminder text; Cathar Commando, Flooded Strand and Mind Stone as one-shot costs on cards played for something else; and Mystic Remora's cumulative upkeep, which is a price paid to KEEP a card rather than a resource converted. Walking Ballista and Hangarback Walker remove counters, not permanents; Drift of Phantasms' transmute and the Eiganjo/Otawara channels are discards. And the Treasure this engine exists to make is spent by sacrificing it, which is the whole of lines[1]. The conclusion survives the correction: there is no sacrifice ENGINE and no aristocrats loop. What this deck converts is an EVENT -- an opponent drawing a card -- which is not a card and cannot be assigned to a stage, so the closed set of eight has no slot for the most characteristic thing about it. WITHDRAWN: 'no goldfish target can price the engine's output: the harness has no opponents to generate the event'. The harness models the event since 2026-10-04; on this deck both channels that read it are off (proposed_goldfish_edits[6]).

COMPLETENESS: 85 distinct entries (100 copies, 33 of them lands) placed across seven stages -- mana 26, ignition 10, fuel 11, conversion 7, output 5, protection 25, wincon 1 = 85. `unassigned` is empty.

unmatched_v1_lines.note: THE NEW ROUTE, AND THE REASON THE SWAP IS STRUCTURAL. Gleaming Splendor reads "Whenever an opponent draws their second card each turn" -- a natural draw step is one card, so with no gift piece out the trigger never fires. Howling Mine's "At the beginning of each player's draw step, if this artifact is untapped, that player draws an additional card" gives every opponent a second card on their own turn, which is one Treasure per opponent per turn cycle from a {1}{W} enchantment -- and that untapped clause is the one switch on the gift, since a tapped Mine hands nobody anything. Kami of the Crescent Moon and Dictate of Kruphix carry that sentence WITHOUT the condition, and Font of Mythos says "two additional cards"; Temple Bell, Mikokoro, Kwain and Loran do it at instant speed on any turn, and The Second Doctor at your end step. Exactly two cards in the 99 carry this trigger (the other is Faerie Mastermind) and exactly three make Treasure (An Offer You Can't Refuse, Gleaming Splendor, Smothering Tithe), enumerated over cards.json oracle text. NOT MEASURED: goldfish_targets.json declares no model_treasures key, and `model-coverage heliod` reports 'model_treasures off' with Gleaming Splendor and Smothering Tithe DARK on it. The harness CAN express this line -- goldfish_turn.py makes GOLDFISH_OPPONENTS (3) Treasure from a second-card trigger when opponent_draws_this_turn >= 2 -- so the gap is a switch, not a missing instrument (proposed_goldfish_edits[6]). Forge has cast the card in one run only: branch splendor-v1's 40-game run 1b132fbb, 9 casts, on a seat (sha badd46c9) that is not this list. Claim, not fact.

THE PILOT ALREADY WROTE THIS LINE. Log 002: "I was overthinking the mana cost — with the treasure and the discount it is two or three, not seven. I waited, got desperate, and the window closed." Treasure is the only mana in this deck that banks across turns, and V12 took the PERMANENTS that make it from one to two (An Offer You Can't Refuse is an instant, and its Treasure goes to the opponent). Smothering Tithe's Treasure can be declined for {2}; Gleaming Splendor's cannot. Forge b0f44e4a (v1.2.1): Smothering Tithe cast 24 times across 120 games -- engine_casts.by_card carries only {cast, activated, discarded} and has no per-game dimension, so that is a cast count and not a count of games. No figure on disk prices Treasure against the {6}{W}: both Treasure makers are DARK in the goldfish. Claim, not fact.

unmatched_v1_lines.note: THE TIMING SPLIT. WITHDRAWN: the previous 'TIMING TRAP', which said the draw-step gifts 'cannot do this ... on yours they contribute {0}' and so made the gift sound half dead. Taken literally it was true, but it ignored the back face's FIRST clause, "You may cast spells as though they had flash." The gate that opens the discount also lifts the sorcery-speed limit. Under Howling Mine an opponent has drawn 2 by the end of their draw step, so every spell you cast on that turn costs {2} less; under Font of Mythos it is {3}. strategic_frame.json says 'the discount is largest on an opponent's turn -- exactly where a draw-go fort spends mana'. This line no longer disagrees with that. What it adds: on an opponent's turn a draw-step gift counts only that one opponent's draws, while Mikokoro's "{2}, {T}: Each player draws a card" on YOUR turn makes three opponents draw, which is {3} off every spell you cast for the rest of that turn. So the split is by WHOSE turn a piece can reach. Howling Mine, Font, Kami, Dictate and Horn of Greed discount only opponents' turns. Temple Bell, Mikokoro, Kwain and Loran activate at instant speed and discount any turn, yours included. The Second Doctor triggers "at the beginning of your end step", so it discounts only what you cast in your own end step. Two of those five say "may" on the opponent's side (Kwain, The Second Doctor). WITHDRAWN: round 2's 'the on-demand pieces discount your own turn and the draw-step pieces discount theirs', which called an end-step trigger on-demand and kept four instant-speed pieces to one turn. Gated on the back face. Forge b0f44e4a (v1.2.1, seat 214af308): engine_casts gives Heliod, the Radiant Dawn cast 91 / activated 44 across 120 games (the front face's only activated ability is the transform), and commander_access reads the back face reached in 35 of 120 games. Claim, not fact.

Stack 002, step 4: with {U} up, Swan Song counters the opponent's instant and Approach remains on the stack and resolves. The stack states its own limit -- Swan Song answers an enchantment, instant or sorcery SPELL and cannot answer an activated or triggered ability. This is the only pairing a passing stack's RESOLUTION supports. engine-facts lists three verified pairings out of 002 -- Approach/Mystical Tutor, Approach/Swan Song, Mystical Tutor/Swan Song -- but Mystical Tutor occurs only in the scenario's premise and in none of the eight resolution steps, so the two pairings that name it are mechanical co-occurrence, not a proven line.

unmatched_v1_lines.note: V12's protection swap, and the line it is bought for. "Other enchantments you control have shroud" covers ten of the eleven enchantments in the 99, Auramancy itself excepted, and Heliod is an enchantment creature -- so the commander, Rhystic Study, Mystic Remora, Smothering Tithe, Gleaming Splendor, Dictate of Kruphix, Teferi's Ageless Insight, Propaganda, Ghostly Prison and Leyline of Anticipation all become untargetable. Lightning Greaves, which it replaced, covered one creature and was the MOST-USED member of the declared protection group in Forge b0f44e4a (v1.2.1, seat 214af308) -- cast 29 times with 41 activations, the only member of that group the AI ever activated. It was not the only member it used, and the whole group has to be named: Leyline of Anticipation was cast 21 times and Karametra's Blessing 9 in the same 120 games, while Teferi's Protection and Guardian of Faith were cast 0. (Cast counts, not game counts.) So the swap costs the group its most-used and only activatable member; it does not cost the deck its only working insurance. THE COST, IF shroud blocks your own targeting as Auramancy's reminder text reads: Karametra's Blessing and Guardian of Faith could no longer be aimed at Heliod while Auramancy is out. Not cited by any stack; open_questions[0], for resolve-stack. Claim, not fact.

The drain half -- and the one DRAIN Forge has ever cast for this deck. wincon:drain is exactly two cards; Scrawling Crawler is cast in all four of this deck's own sim records (46 in b0f44e4a (v1.2.1, seat 214af308)) and Psychosis Crawler in none (0 cast, 10 discarded in b0f44e4a). Those four runs played v1.0.0 (996adb84), v1.2.1 (b0f44e4a, 4b0e1964) and V5 (92280ee6, seat 2d7f07f9), never the current one. It is NOT the only output card Forge ran: in the same 120 games Walking Ballista was cast 52 / activated 99, Hangarback Walker 37 / activated 21 and Secure the Wastes 20. Scrawling Crawler triggers on OPPONENT draws, which is what the draw-step gift multiplies; Howling Mine was cast 27 times in that run, and the logs do not attribute a drain to a specific gift piece. The declared component that prices the pair -- 'Table draw engine plus a draw-triggered drain, both drawn' -- reads 0.383 assembled and 0.209 by turn six, the file's lowest, because the drain half is a two-card any_of and the first any_of omits Scrawling Crawler although it is itself a table draw engine (proposed_goldfish_edits[4]). The goldfish counts neither Crawler's drain: model-coverage lists both DARK. Claim, not fact.

unmatched_v1_lines.note: UNSETTLED. The back face reduces generic cost, so a discount should allow a larger X on Stroke of Genius, Braingeyser, Prosperity, Skyscribing, Mathemagics, Secure the Wastes, Walking Ballista or Hangarback Walker. Whether X is chosen before or after the reduction applies is open_questions[2]; nothing on disk settles it, and the declared component 'An X-spell finisher drawn (the mana sink the discount pays for)' rests entirely on it at 0.838 assembled. THE ROUTE BACK, via Mystical Tutor, which is one of thirteen instants at mana value two or less in the 99 -- An Offer You Can't Refuse, Arcane Denial, Counterspell, Cyclonic Rift, Disenchant, Dovin's Veto, Enlightened Tutor, Karametra's Blessing, Mystical Tutor, Path to Exile, Secure the Wastes, Swan Song, Swords to Plowshares (enumerated from cards.json type lines and mana values). Imprinted, "{2}, {T}: You may copy the exiled card" puts Approach on top every turn without spending the Tutor. The Scepter's ability is not a spell and is never discounted by the back face. Whether an Approach drawn this way still counts as "cast from your hand" is not in doubt -- you cast it from hand after drawing it -- but no stack has run the line. deck-facts finds exactly one combo line contained in this 99 and the Scepter is not in it. Claim, not fact.

The arrow the whole mana base exists to draw, and the one the figures argue with. {6}{W} twice is fourteen mana on two separate turns; goldfish mean_available_mana crosses seven between turn 7 (6.594) and turn 8 (7.383) on the current list. Forge b0f44e4a (v1.2.1): Approach cast 39 times across 120 games, and 12 of the run's 20 wins carry won_by "effect of 'Approach of the Second Sun'". THE RUN HAS NO SECOND-CAST COUNTER: a second cast that was countered would appear in the 39 and in no won_by entry, so second casts are bounded at twelve or more and were never measured. Claim, not fact.

The largest multiplier in the deck. Font of Mythos is "that player draws TWO additional cards" in each player's draw step, so it adds six opponent draws a round cycle; Consecrated Sphinx draws you two on every opponent draw. Counting each opponent's base draw, the cycle is nine opponent draws and eighteen cards. Only Font also feeds Gleaming Splendor and Faerie Mastermind: every opponent draws three in their own draw step. Sphinx's eighteen cards are YOUR draws, so none is an opponent's second card and they trigger neither (WITHDRAWN: 'both halves also feed' them). Forge b0f44e4a (v1.2.1, seat 214af308): Font cast 26 times, Sphinx 25, across 120 games (cast counts, not game counts -- engine_casts has no per-game dimension); nothing in the record says how often they overlapped. In the goldfish, Sphinx is DARK (model_discard off) while Font of Mythos is 'seen' (draw, target) -- so the goldfish counts Font's opponent draws and never prices Sphinx's response to them (WITHDRAWN: 'Both are DARK'). Claim, not fact.

v1_stages.label: WHAT PAYS FOR {6}{W} TWICE, AND IT IS SHORT
v1_stages.what_it_does:
33 land copies in 18 entries, seven rocks, two Medallions. The bill is Approach of the Second Sun's, twice: {6}{W} on two separate turns. mana_analysis (sha f7e21dc6, model f5b4b19d2254) reads 24 W and 27 U total sources against a Karsten 36 apiece -- "the target is a yardstick, not a possibility, in a 33-land deck", that file's own words -- with lands-only on-curve 0.580 W / 0.667 U, and 0.548 / 0.639 once Skycloud Expanse is set aside as the one gated source. deck-audit reads mana-base UNDER (33 against the control band 37-39 the frame's archetype sets) and colour-sources UNDER, worst colour -12.

V12's third swap lives here: one Plains to one Island. Pips are 0.611 U / 0.389 W; land sources are 23 U / 20 W. The change moves the lighter-pip colour's basic to the heavier one; it does not close a 12-source gap and nothing claims it does.

goldfish mean_available_mana_by_turn crosses seven between turn 7 (6.594) and turn 8 (7.383), and the commander's discount is not in it: goldfish_profiles.cost_reduction() returns None for Heliod, so every mana figure in this artifact is a floor. benchmark missed_land_drop_rate 0.2466, worst turn six; land_drop_hit_rate falls 0.871 (t3) to 0.564 (t6).

Mind Stone taps for {C} and pays the {3} of the flip exactly as Sol Ring and Thought Vessel do; the declared flip component omits it (proposed_goldfish_edits[3]). Pearl and Sapphire Medallion reduce SPELL costs and tap for nothing, so they cannot pay any part of an activated ability.

v1_stages.label: THE GIFT -- THE TABLE HAS TO BE DRAWING
v1_stages.what_it_does:
The first thing that has to happen, and the one thing this deck reliably does. Every card here hands cards to players who are not you: eight say "each player" or "that player" (Howling Mine, Font of Mythos, Kami of the Crescent Moon, Dictate of Kruphix, Temple Bell, Mikokoro, The Second Doctor, Horn of Greed -- enumerated by oracle text over cards.json), Kwain says "each player may draw", and Loran alone says "you and target opponent".

The declared component 'Table draw engine online (opponents are drawing)' is these ten plus Scrawling Crawler and measures 0.917 assembled, 0.821 by turn six, mean turn 2.449 -- the highest assembled rate and earliest mean turn of the eleven targets, 0.574 in an opening seven. It is a DRAWN rate: goldfish meta.card_advantage.draw_not_modelled names four of these ten (Howling Mine, Kwain, Loran, The Second Doctor).

WHY IT IS IGNITION AND NOT DECORATION. Five conversion-side cards read an opponent drawing. Two of them -- Faerie Mastermind and Gleaming Splendor, the only two cards in the 99 carrying "an opponent draws their second card each turn" -- cannot fire off a natural draw step, which is one card. They need a piece from this stage. Smothering Tithe, Consecrated Sphinx and Scrawling Crawler fire on ANY opponent draw; this stage multiplies them.

WHERE IT FIRES DECIDES WHICH TURN IS CHEAP. Howling Mine, Font, Kami and Dictate fire in each player's draw step, Horn on each land drop: they discount an OPPONENT's turn (the back face also gives flash), never yours. Temple Bell, Mikokoro, Kwain and Loran activate at instant speed and discount any turn. Also on YOUR turn: The Second Doctor (end step), Scrawling Crawler (upkeep), Prosperity, Skyscribing, Splendor's and Mastermind's activations, and Arcane Denial if the next upkeep is yours.

v1_stages.label: YOUR OWN CARDS, AND TWO ROUTES TO THE WIN
v1_stages.what_it_does:
V12 cut Alhammarret's Archive from this stage and put nothing back. After the swap exactly ONE card in the 99 doubles your own draw -- Teferi's Ageless Insight ("draw two cards instead", enumerated over cards.json oracle text). The deck traded a fuel doubler for a conversion piece, so this stage got thinner and conversion got wider.

TWO ROUTES to Approach of the Second Sun, and two tutors that look like routes and are not. The routes: Mystical Tutor ({U}, an instant or sorcery to the top) and Long-Term Plans ({2}{U}, any card, third from the top). The non-routes: Enlightened Tutor finds an artifact or enchantment only, and Drift of Phantasms' transmute finds a card of mana value three -- Approach is a seven-mana sorcery, so neither can fetch it. deck-audit's tutors axis counts four; two of the four cannot fetch the deck's only win condition. The declared component 'Win condition access' is exactly Approach plus the two routes: 0.560 assembled, 0.380 by turn six, mean turn 4.436.

The five X-draw spells (Braingeyser, Stroke of Genius, Prosperity, Skyscribing, Mathemagics) are the mana sink the back-face discount is supposed to pay for; whether the discount buys a larger X is open_questions[2] and nothing on disk settles it. Isochron Scepter imprints any of 13 instants at mana value two or less, Mystical Tutor among them (lines[7]).

v1_stages.label: SEVEN CARDS ON ONE TABLE STATE -- FOUR READ THE DRAW, TWO READ THE CAST, ONE READS THE COUNT
v1_stages.what_it_does:
THE ENGINE PROPER. Exactly five cards in the 99 trigger on "an opponent draws" (Consecrated Sphinx, Faerie Mastermind, Gleaming Splendor, Scrawling Crawler, Smothering Tithe -- enumerated over cards.json oracle text; Scrawling Crawler is placed in output because its payoff is life loss). ONE can be declined: Smothering Tithe lets the player pay {2}. The other four are unconditional.

GLEAMING SPLENDOR IS V12's SWAP. "Whenever an opponent draws their second card each turn, you create a Treasure token" is Faerie Mastermind's trigger word for word, with Treasure where Mastermind has a card. With a draw-step gift online, every opponent's own turn gives them a second card. Its "{2}{W}: Two target players each draw a card" is an activated ability, and an ability is not a spell, so Heliod's back face never discounts it.

Rhystic Study and Mystic Remora read a CAST, not a draw, and both can be paid off. Heliod's back face reads the same table state -- "{1} less to cast for each card your opponents have drawn this turn".

WHAT THE GOLDFISH SEES OF THIS STAGE: almost nothing. model-coverage lists Consecrated Sphinx, Faerie Mastermind and Rhystic Study DARK on model_discard and Gleaming Splendor and Smothering Tithe DARK on model_treasures -- five of the seven, and both channels are off -- while cost_reduction() returns None for the commander. The declared component 'Heliod down with an asymmetric card engine' (0.836 assembled, 0.601 by turn six, mean turn 5.355, commander-gated) measures DRAWING one of seven; nothing on disk measures what they produce (proposed_goldfish_edits[6]).
cards: Heliod, the Radiant Dawn // Heliod, the Warped Eclipse

v1_stages.label: WHAT IT ACTUALLY PRODUCES -- VALUE, AND A KILL ONLY RARELY
v1_stages.what_it_does:
Scrawling Crawler drains one life per opponent draw; Psychosis Crawler drains one per YOUR draw and is a body sized to your hand; Secure the Wastes, Walking Ballista and Hangarback Walker turn leftover mana into counters or tokens.

WHAT THE GOLDFISH SAYS, AND WHAT IT CANNOT. On the current list: kill_by_turn_6 0.000, kill_by_turn_8 0.003, kill_by_turn_10 0.106, no kill by turn ten 0.894, median kill turn 10; mean_board_power_by_turn 6.645 at turn ten. But model-coverage lists BOTH Crawlers DARK (on model_discard, which is off), so that is a combat-only reading in which neither drain is counted -- a floor under the drains, not a verdict on them. The declared pairing 'Table draw engine plus a draw-triggered drain, both drawn' is the file's lowest at 0.383 assembled and 0.209 by turn six.

FORGE b0f44e4a (120 games, heliod seat sha 214af308 = v1.2.1, two lists behind): Walking Ballista cast 52 / activated 99, Scrawling Crawler cast 46, Hangarback Walker cast 37 / activated 21, Secure the Wastes cast 20, Psychosis Crawler cast 0 and discarded 10 -- held and passed over, the CLAUDE.md floor condition; it reads cast 0 in all four of this deck's own sim records. Of the run's 20 heliod wins, won_by gives 12 to "effect of 'Approach of the Second Sun'" and 8 to "all opponents have lost". The seat is credited with 7 opponent eliminations across the 120 games, all by damage (baylen-tokens 4, abaddon 3).

The reading: this stage produces value and kills rarely -- 7 eliminations in 120 Forge games on v1.2.1, and a 0.106 combat kill by turn ten in the goldfish with the drains uncounted. Approach is the only kill the deck is BUILT around.

v1_stages.label: TWENTY-FIVE CARDS BUYING TURNS FOR A SEVEN-DROP
v1_stages.what_it_does:
GREATER AURAMANCY IS V12's SECOND SWAP, and it is not a like-for-like for Lightning Greaves. It says SHROUD, not hexproof: "Other enchantments you control have shroud." There are eleven enchantments in the 99 (Dictate of Kruphix, Ghostly Prison, Gleaming Splendor, Greater Auramancy, Heliod, Leyline of Anticipation, Mystic Remora, Propaganda, Rhystic Study, Smothering Tithe, Teferi's Ageless Insight -- enumerated from type lines). Auramancy covers the other TEN, and Heliod is an enchantment creature, so the commander is covered. Log 001 lost to exactly what this answers: "I cast Swords to Plowshares, Alex redirected it onto Heliod. Engine offline from there."

THE COST NOBODY DECLARED, if shroud blocks your own targeting, as Auramancy's reminder text reads ("can't be the target of spells or abilities") and no stack has yet cited. Karametra's Blessing targets a creature you control and Guardian of Faith phases out "other target creatures you control"; on that reading, neither could be aimed at Heliod while Auramancy is out. Teferi's Protection does not target. open_questions[0], for resolve-stack.

EIGHT true counterspells, enumerated twice (deck-facts role 'counterspell' = 8; oracle search for "counter target" = the same 8). Declared 'Free or cheap interaction held': 0.886 assembled, 0.718 by turn six. deck-audit on the control band: interaction AT 14 (12-15), protection AT 5 (5-7), sweepers UNDER 2 (5-7). Kefnet needs seven cards in hand; four cards remove your maximum hand size (Decanter of Endless Water, Reliquary Tower, The Second Doctor, Thought Vessel).

v1_stages.label: ONE CARD, CAST TWICE, AND NOTHING ELSE
v1_stages.what_it_does:
"If this spell was cast from your hand and you've cast another spell named Approach of the Second Sun this game, you win the game." One card. The stage has a single point of failure by construction, and every other stage exists to buy the turns for it.

WHAT IS PROVEN: stack 002 passes and shows the second cast winning through one counterspell window with Swan Song held. What is NOT proven is the route to it -- Mystical Tutor appears in 002 only as premise (graveyard, game_history) and in none of the eight resolution steps, so the tutor-to-Approach line stays a claim.

WHAT IT COSTS: {6}{W} twice, fourteen mana across two turns, against a goldfish that crosses seven mean available mana between turn 7 (6.594) and turn 8 (7.383) with the discount unmodelled. Forge b0f44e4a (v1.2.1, 120 games): Approach cast 39 times and discarded 7, and 12 of heliod's 20 wins carry won_by "effect of 'Approach of the Second Sun'". THE RUN COUNTS NO SECOND CASTS. A countered second cast lands in the 39 and in no won_by entry, so the record bounds second casts at TWELVE OR MORE. Summary: 20 wins in 99 decided, mean round 20.9.

WHAT NO ARTIFACT MEASURES: the actual win is Approach in hand AND seven mana available on two separate turns. The declared component scores 0.560 by counting a hand that DREW any of three cards, two of which are tutors. NO RATIO BETWEEN THAT AND ANY FORGE FIGURE IS STATED HERE: 0.560 is a 10,000-iteration goldfish DRAW rate over ten turns on the current list, and every Approach count above is an AI CAST count over a mean 20.9 rounds on a seat two lists behind. open_questions[5].

v1_map_disagreements.component: CONVERSION -- the five cards that read one event
v1_map_disagreements.why: The most valuable disagreement on this deck, and it has now SURVIVED A CHANGE OF EMBEDDING. Gleaming Splendor and Faerie Mastermind carry the byte-identical trigger "Whenever an opponent draws their second card each turn". The CardBERT map puts Splendor in city-0 hood ANY-COLOUR MANA beside Smothering Tithe, Command Tower and Arcane Signet, and Mastermind in city-1 BODIES THAT DRAW beside Heliod and Consecrated Sphinx. The previous map, built in embeddings_ability.npy (git daaa3025), split the same pair the same way -- Splendor with the Treasure makers, Mastermind with card flow. Two spaces, one answer: the map files by the PAYOFF clause and the type line, never by the trigger. No card in this group states what the group is for, so the engine proper is invisible to a reader of the constellation.

The cartographer's own note says this space 'clusters this deck mostly by card TYPE and colour, not by job', and this stage is where that costs most: white removal and wraths to city-3, counterspells to city-4, enchantments to city-5, blue cards to city-1 -- while the deck uses all 25 for one job, buying turns until a seven-drop can be cast twice. An Offer You Can't Refuse and Arcane Denial, two of the eight counterspells, sit in TUTORS AND BIG DRAWS ('likely because both hand opponents cards', the cartographer's words); Drift of Phantasms sits there on its transmute, not on the flying blocker the deck declares it as; Kefnet sits in BODIES THAT DRAW on his draw ability. city-4 THE NO is the only city wholly inside this stage.

v1_map_disagreements.component: WINCON -- Approach of the Second Sun
v1_map_disagreements.why: A one-card stage in one city, so the scatter is trivially coherent; the disagreement is in the neighbourhood. Approach shares hood WRATHS, EXILES, ESCAPES with eight cards, none of which can win a game, because the embedding reads a white sorcery beside white spells. The cartographer saw the exit and wrote it into the city's name; the space did not. Supersedes the previous entry, which placed Approach in a 'Finishers' hood beside value engines on the old map.

Measured, not judged: engine-facts' scatter reads the declared eleven-card gift group as 3 cities (THE ECONOMY 6, THE DEEP DIG 4, ANSWERS AND THE EXIT 1), and only 2 of 12 components sit in one city -- both of them the two-Crawler any_of. The split is by type: the artifacts and Mikokoro in HUG HARDWARE, the creatures and Dictate in city-1, Loran in NONCREATURE ANSWERS on its enters-trigger ('destroy up to one target artifact or enchantment'). WITHDRAWN from the previous entry: 'Mikokoro alone in Mana, because it is a land' and 'the thinnest cut-across in this file'. The rebuilt map files Mikokoro WITH the gift, by function, and splits the stage elsewhere.

v1_map_disagreements.component: MANA -- the rocks and the Medallions
v1_map_disagreements.why: Two cities: 15 of 26 in city-2, 11 in city-0, and the seven rocks split three ways -- Azorius Signet and Talisman with the lands, Sol Ring, Thought Vessel and Mind Stone in HUG HARDWARE, Arcane Signet and Decanter in ANY-COLOUR MANA. WITHDRAWN: the previous entry's 'WHERE THE MAP IS RIGHT' about the Medallions. The rebuilt map puts Pearl and Sapphire Medallion in HUG HARDWARE beside Sol Ring, Thought Vessel and Mind Stone -- the three COLOURLESS rocks. All seven rocks pay the generic {3} of '{3}{U/P}: Transform Heliod'; a Medallion cannot pay any of it, because it taps for nothing. goldfish_targets correctly omits both Medallions from every target; the map now files them with the cards they cannot replace.
